title: Responsible AI: Risk, Impact & Governance
interviewAnswer: Responsible AI means identifying who can be harmed, how failures are measured, what human oversight exists, and how risks are monitored throughout the lifecycle. I treat it as an engineering requirement, not a final compliance checklist.
why: Model quality metrics do not capture every business, legal or societal failure mode. High-stakes systems need explicit risk ownership.
intuition: Ask not only “does it work?” but “for whom can it fail, what happens when it fails, and who can detect/override it?”
deepDive: A practical lifecycle includes mapping intended use/misuse, measuring risk, documenting limitations, testing subgroups/edge cases, governance and monitoring after deployment. Frameworks such as NIST AI RMF help organize this work.
workedExample: For a recommendation system, measure not only ranking quality but also exposure concentration, subgroup performance, feedback-loop effects and whether users can understand or override consequential recommendations.
commonMistakes: Treating fairness/safety as a one-time pre-launch test.
Assuming a high aggregate metric implies low risk for every subgroup/use case.
followUps: What belongs in a model card?
When should a human stay in the loop?
production: Production systems need incident response, audit trails, explicit fallback behavior and ownership for model-risk decisions.
